newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-MEXICO, DOMINICAN REPUBLIC TO DUEL FOR CARIBBEAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MEXICO, DOMINICAN REPUBLIC TO DUEL FOR CARIBBEAN TITLE.

text.p: Defending champions Mexico and the Dominican Republic will square off Sunday for the Caribbean Series baseball championship after home run driven victories on Saturday.

Both Mexico, represented by the Tomateros de Culiacan (Culiacan Tomato Growers), and the Dominican Republic's Aguilas de Cibao (Cibao Eagles) take 3-2 records into the final game of the four-nation, round-robin tournament after breaking a four-way, 2-2 deadlock with Saturday's victories.
Mexico upset Puerto Rico 10-6 by riding the bat of designated hitter Matt Stark, who stroked two home runs.
In the earlier game, Luis Polonia slammed a two-run homer in the bottom of the ninth to lift the Dominican Republic to an 11-9 victory over Venezuela's Navegantes de Magallanes (Magellan Navigators).
Polonia, who played last season for the Atlanta Braves, drove a fastball from losing relief pitcher Jimmy Myers over the centerfield fence to snap a 9-9 tie.
"I wanted to take a hard swing, not for a home run but for an extra-base hit, and the ball just went," said Polonia, whose game-winning blast was the fifth home run of the game.
The slugfest saw the Dominican Republic pound out 14 hits and Venezuela 15.

New York Yankees utility infielder Luis Sojo had belted a home run to left in the top of the eighth that put Venezuela ahead 9-8. But Guillermo Garcia answered with his second homer of the game, a solo blast in the bottom of the inning to knot the score at 9-9.
Garcia hit a three run homer in the fifth to cap a four-run rally after his team had trailed 8-4.
Dario Veras got the win for the Dominican Republic.
In the second game, Mexico's Mario Valdez hit an RBI single to left in the sixth that broke a 4-4 deadlock.
Stark's second home run an inning later made it 6-4 and Ever Magallanes's solo blast keyed a four-run eighth for a commanding 10-4 lead that made a winner out of former major leaguer Teddy Higueras.

Roberto Alomar and Alex Diaz led off the bottom of the ninth with back-to-back home runs for Puerto Rico to pull within 10-6. But Mexican reliever Ricardo Rincon ended the rally, earning his second save of the series.
Mexico's starting pitcher Sunday, Martin Hernandez, is on a roll his team hopes will give them another Caribbean title.
He won all five of his playoff starts to lead Culiacan to the Mexican Pacific League title and a Caribbean Series berth. He then beat Venezuela in Tuesday's series opener.
The Dominican Republic will send San Francisco Giants starter Julian Tavarez to the mound, although he was roughed up in his first start against Puerto Rico Tuesday.
